decisions.rationale: Plan §5.1/§5.3 requires the Backend protocol to expose artifact_builder() and to have no compile/compile_all hook. The draft removes both methods from the Protocol and adds artifact_builder(kernel_contract, math, kernel_names), so the only way to obtain a builder is the factory the plan mandates.
evidence: AST/grep: after the draft the only remaining `def compile(`/`def compile_all(` in the tree are the runtime primitives tcenv/backends/metal/runtime.py::MetalContext.compile and ::MetalContext.compile_all plus two test stubs; no Backend implementation keeps the removed hook.
Plan §2.1 row 3 lists Backend.compile/compile_all as an R3 deletion; this draft performs exactly that deletion and nothing else on the protocol.
r3_requirements: Keep the factory as the only entry; R3 must not re-add a convenience compile wrapper for any caller.
R3 must add the structural check that no Backend subclass defines compile/compile_all, by AST rather than by hasattr only.

decisions.rationale: The Metal backend becomes a pure factory returning MetalSourceBuilder configured with the contract, math mode and declared kernel names. That matches §5.1 (factory takes Specialization + candidate math/names, no shell/path/command).
evidence: The factory passes only kernel_contract/math/kernel_names into MetalSourceBuilder; it accepts no arbitrary command, path or build string.
tests/support/npu_sim/fake_backend.py migrates the only other Backend implementation to the same shape, so the protocol change is not Metal-only in practice.
r3_requirements: R1 gives the factory the registered LoweringProfile name; R3 must keep the factory from recomputing lowering configuration.
R3 must prove the factory is reached from evaluate/xcworker/probes/profile/fill (spy on backend.artifact_builder), not a directly constructed builder.

symbols: native descriptor kernel_names/kernels for multi-stage builds
decisions.rationale: These parts concentrate the source→pipeline call in one builder method and let one build own a multi-stage pipeline set, which is what §5.1/§5.2 want. The same file also adds MetalSourceBuilder.compile_source, which is discarded (D-D3).
evidence: _compile_assembled is the only place in the builder that calls MetalContext.compile/compile_all; §5.2 makes MetalSourceBuilder._compile_assembled the sole legitimate owner of those calls.

tcenv/backends/metal/runtime.py::MetalContext.compile_all calls self.compile for the first name, so the draft's 1-name branch (context.compile) and the multi-name branch (context.compile_all) are behaviourally the same call sequence.

candidate_sha256 is unaffected: SourceBundle carries the candidate bytes and build() assembles the contract header internally, so provenance.source_sha256 stays the candidate text (F-3 / §3 identity table).
r3_requirements: Delete MetalSourceBuilder.compile_source (D-D3) so the primitive has exactly one caller inside the builder.
Replace the MetalKernelSet + getattr(handle, 'kernels') convention with an explicit typed handle-set contract in the neutral model; do not keep two handle vocabularies.

Add the §5.1 BuildError attachments (typed BuildProvenance with artifact_set_digest=null, assembled_sha256) at the compile-failure site; the draft sets report_detail but attaches no provenance (see X-2).
Move the typed profile acquisition ahead of any candidate-level compile judgement (non-UTF-8 path, X-1).

decisions.rationale: _evaluate_in_process stops calling backend.assemble/compile/compile_all and instead asks the backend for its builder and calls build(). The compile_error report text keeps its pre-refactor shape (rewritten diagnostic only) and the candidate bytes remain the SOURCE artifact.
evidence: The builder receives SourceBundle(kernel_source.encode('utf-8')) and task_contract=contract; the contract header is assembled inside build(), so candidate_sha256 still describes exactly what the model wrote.
Only BuildError(error_class='compile') is mapped to status=compile_error; other classes are re-raised, matching the legacy 'toolchain failures are not candidate failures' rule (§5.3 item 4).
The report keeps rep.compile = {ok: False, errors: ...} with rewrite_compiler_lines applied inside the builder, i.e. the same text as HEAD's evaluate path.
r3_requirements: Keep exactly one build() call per candidate and use BuildOutcome.executable_handles() only for local handles.
Map BuildError(deadline) to timeout before any crash path if a local deadline is ever introduced (§5.3 item 3); today local callers pass no deadline.
Pass deadline_monotonic=None explicitly at every local call site (R3 spy assertion).

decisions.rationale: Profiling used to compile through ctx.compile/ctx.compile_all, i.e. a second source→pipeline path. The draft routes it through the same factory and build(), keeps the multi-stage ordering from the parsed taic-launch spec, and stops calling assemble itself.
evidence: After the draft xcworker.py contains no ctx.compile/ctx.compile_all and builds the name list from spec.stages, matching what evaluate.py passes to the builder.
The multi-stage launch is still one build; by_name ordering is preserved for stage execution.
r3_requirements: R3 must spy backend.artifact_builder -> build for the profiling path and assert one outcome for the multi-stage launch.

decisions.rationale: report_detail separates the builder-facing classification message from the report diagnostic text, which is needed to keep the local compile_error text byte-identical. The live-handle invariant closes a real hole: two records that both omit the handle compare equal only because the handle is excluded from equality and digests.
evidence: BuildOutcome.__post_init__ now rejects an outcome whose evidence.native and bundle.native both carry handle=None, so a handle-less 'success' cannot be constructed.
tests/backends/metal/test_source_builder.py::test_one_build_outcome_must_name_one_live_executable extends the existing invariant test with the both-None case.
executable_handles() is the single unwrap point used by evaluate.py and xcworker.py.
r3_requirements: Replace the getattr(handle, 'kernels') heuristic with an explicit handle-set contract (X-3); a duck-typed convention is a second vocabulary.
Keep BuildError as the failure attachment; do not add a second outcome DTO (§2.1 row 11).

decisions.rationale: The test file follows the protocol change: the legacy comparison now calls the runtime primitive directly (ctx.compile) instead of the deleted backend hook, and the stub backends grow a compile method on the context. Placement is correct (tests/backends/metal).

defects.title: handle set is a duck-typed convention, not a neutral type
defects.detail: getattr(native.handle, 'kernels', None) decides whether a handle is a set. Any handle object that happens to expose kernels changes the meaning, and the neutral model gains an implicit second vocabulary.

defects.title: internal fill kernel still compiles through the runtime primitive

defects.title: experiments tree still compiles through the runtime primitive

defects.title: multi-stage native descriptor grows new keys

defects.title: fake builder has no compile-failure path
